title: rootless: close /dev/fd after scanning inherited fds on FreeBSD
body:
When building container images with podman inside a FreeBSD jail, every layer unpack was failing with "ApplyLayer ... operation not permitted".

Tracing it down, the FreeBSD constructor opens /dev/fd to check which descriptors are open before the Go runtime starts, and never closes the directory stream (unlike the Linux version). That leaves an open directory fd inherited by child processes, including storage-applyLayer. Inside a jail, FreeBSD refuses chroot(2) while a directory fd is open (kern.chroot_allow_open_directories=1 by default), so the unpack aborts.

Call closedir() after the scan to close the /dev/fd handle before the runtime starts.
